newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kinkel says EMU to start on time.
newsitem.headline: Kinkel says EMU to start on time.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said on Wednesday there was no doubt that European monetary union (EMU) would start as planned in January 1999.
"In my view the point of no return has been passed," Kinkel said in an interview with Die Welt. The interview was released by his ministry in advance of its Thursday publication.
Kinkel said Germany had a realistic chance of meeting the EMU criteria, and that currency union without the participation of Germany and France was unthinkable.
"If we do not meet the criteria, there will be no euro. But that would be disastrous for Germany. There would be a massive revaluation of the mark," he said.
The current calm on financial markets reflects the recognition that Germany will do everything it must to make the grade for EMU, he said.
